title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + hysteresis during regional failover
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: In the most recent incident we observed rapid oscillation (thrashing) in the SLO enforcer during partial regional outages. The enforcer's backoff/hysteresis logic and regional failover ordering allowed multiple unhealthy regions to be selected and then immediately unselected leading to cascades and excess load on fallback paths. This hotfix tightens hysteresis windows, adds a short randomized jitter to backoff timers, and ensures deterministic region ordering for failovers to prevent flip-flopping. Changes: 1) Increase hysteresis window for SLO breach evaluation from 30s -> 120s for regional decisions. 2) Introduce backoff jitter (20-50ms per enforcer instance) to avoid synchronized retries. 3) Add a deterministic region-priority comparator with soft affinity so that when two regions are comparable we prefer the same order across nodes. 4) Guard rails in the enforcer to limit concurrent regional failover attempts to 1 per cluster per 60s. 5) Add metrics and tracing spans for hysteresis decisions and backoff events. Rollout: Hotfix is targeted to hosted and dedicated control planes; config defaults remain conservative for Private customers but can be adjusted via feature flag. Testing: unit tests for comparator and jitter, integration canary in us-west-2 with mirrored traffic for 2h, and chaos-runner simulation against the regional-failover harness. Linear: ENG-2381 (primary), ENG-2410 (follow-up to add per-customer tuning). This PR is intended as an urgent stability fix to reduce SLO enforcer thrashing and improve graceful degradation during regional instability.
